evidence: All five dimension prompts open the live app through the browser tool and forbid every non-browser scoring path. (1) Each of the five prompt.md files begins at line 1 with 'Open http://localhost:3000 using Playwright.' and continues 'Use rendered UI and ordinary browser-observed product data only. Never inspect app source, bundles, filesystem, database files or implementation code. No shell or private-file probes. Discover routes and controls by intent, not assumed names.' (gates/render/prompt.md:1, gates/constraints/prompt.md:1, scored/functional/prompt.md:1 [adds 'No shell. Use restart_app only if your criterion says so, and then only once.'], scored/polish/prompt.md:1, scored/visual/prompt.md:1). This is stricter than the template, which only says 'Evaluate the live application at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright MCP.' (2) Every judge.toml wires [[judge.mcp_servers]] name='playwright', command='playwright-mcp', args ['--headless','--isolated','--executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium','--no-sandbox'] (render/constraints/functional/polish/visual judge.toml lines 8-12), pinned @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 in tests/Dockerfile:19. Functional also wires the verifier restart server (judge.toml:14-18). (3) No scoring path can be satisfied from first paint or memory. Render needs a wrong-password refusal and then a real sign-in (render/judge.toml:25). Constraints needs a UI add, a reload and an independent-context Observer readback (constraints/judge.toml:51; prompt.md:9). Functional, polish and visual each repeat a write-then-independent-context-readback Global browser gate (functional:15-17, polish:11-12, visual:11-12). Visual must also walk the Board, card details, Noor's 120-message conversation, Activity and a candidate view in an independent context (visual/prompt.md:14), so it cannot grade from a first paint. Functional and polish need timed multi-context observations in browser_run_code_unsafe (functional:29, polish:18). The functional and polish 'Report every step' sections (functional:31-33, polish:20-22) fail skipped steps, and visual:16-18 does the same, which addresses Colderwater lesson 9 against memory or assumed passes. (4) Runtime ordering: test.sh starts the app and waits for readiness on 127.0.0.1:3000 (lines 104-125) before rewardkit runs (lines 203-227), and substitutes {app_context} into every prompt (lines 195-201), so the judge reaches a live app. app_context.md:4 gives URL http://localhost:3000. (5) Colderwater lesson 13 (row 25 portal flag: no public internet address in judge prompts): a grep of every URL under tests/ finds only http://localhost:3000 (app_context.md:4 and the five prompt.md:1 lines) and http://127.0.0.1:3000 (test.sh:48,136). No public host is used for navigation or grading. The '@hireops.example' and '@candidates.example' strings are account identifiers on the reserved .example TLD, used as login and form data, not addresses to visit. Lesson 6 (checker-not-fixer in every prompt.md) is present at line 7 of all five prompts. Lesson 8 (hold the modifier key during the click) is at app_context.md:33-35. (6) Counterexample attempts. A broken app that could pass: a static or first-paint shell fails render, which needs a sign-in state change, and fails constraints and the scored gates, which need a server-backed cross-context readback. A source-only judge path is explicitly forbidden. A conforming alternative that could fail: the prompts avoid assumed routes and selectors ('Discover routes and controls by intent'; app_context.md:37-38). Request replays are limited to requests the UI was observed to make (functional:25), so a different but valid route layout is not penalized. Neither attempt produced a credible defect for this row. (7) Tool-name feasibility: browser_run_code_unsafe is named in the prompts. Historical evidence (scripts/check_hireops_mcp.cjs:72-78, which asserts tools/list includes it, and NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md:316) supports its availability under the pinned MCP. That evidence is not in this round's raw-evidence-index, and the tool's feasibility belongs mainly to other rows. Notes (not defects for this row): (a) The raw-evidence-index says full configured grading is absent. No configured judge transcript in this round shows the judge actually navigating, so this verdict rests on prompt and wiring content, which is exactly what this row checks. Compliance at run time is unmeasured and is not claimed. (b) test.sh:85-86 leaves /app world-readable. The claude-code judge could technically read the source, and only the prompt prohibition prevents it. This is template-controlled harness behaviour, so it is not to be edited here. (c) The gate prompts (render, constraints) lack a 'Report every step' section. Each has one short criterion and the NOT EXERCISED rule, so this is not a row-25 defect.
